code_changes.peer attribution (receipts/verify.py, ch: _peer_entity considers only companies the same draft names (verify.named_in_draft) and those its context line names, never the whole universe; context companies are kept for attribution even when the context stops steering period resolution; named_in_draft never fails a check
code_changes.entity safety (receipts/store.py, verify: a ticker of two letters or fewer or in WORD_TICKERS never resolves by itself; free-text scans (a draft, an Ask question) also skip single words in WORD_NAMES; a company whose own name is a word ticker (Flex, Ball, Dow, Fox, Pool) resolves only with a legal suffix ('Flex Ltd.'), and a bare 'Flex' gets an everyday-word explanation; aliases are looked up through a cached index; SEC registrant tags ('/NEW/', '/DE/') are stripped for new aliases; known_companies lists the store's companies
code_changes.DEI label reuse (receipts/ingest.py): a filing that reuses an earlier filing's DEI label for the same period one year later gets the next fiscal year's label when that label is free; any other conflict still keeps the earlier filing
code_changes.component revenue (receipts/ingest.py): a RevenueFromContractWithCustomer figure stands for revenue only when it is at least half of both the operating expenses and the cost of revenue the same filing reports for the period; bank fee income and REIT non-lease income are slices (Fifth Third about $150M a quarter against $1.2B noninterest expense; Camden $13M for 2025 against $567M cost of revenue). The cost-of-revenue yardstick was added after the first final gates, when Camden's three annual figures (stored 6 times) were found to have survived the operating-expense test; Camden was re-ingested
